title: Reservations and Waitlist Priority for Safe Deposit Boxes
content:
A reservation for one of the bank's Safe Deposit Boxes is recorded against a size and a branch, and places the customer on that branch's waitlist for that size.

## The standards a reservation is measured against

**Age.** The customer must be at least 18 years old on the reservation date.

**Branch.** A size can be reserved only at a branch where that size is installed.

## The order in which boxes are offered

Waitlisted customers are offered boxes in the order of their reservation dates, the earliest reservation first. An offer is never made ahead of an earlier reservation for the same size at the same branch.

## What settles the age standard

The age is settled by the date of birth the bank's records hold for that customer, read before the reservation is recorded and matched to the customer the reservation is being taken for. The customer's own statement of their age does not settle it.

## Boundary of the age standard

The standard is met by a customer who is at least 18 on the reservation date, so a customer whose recorded date of birth makes them exactly 18 years old on the day the reservation is taken meets it. A customer whose recorded date of birth would make them 18 only on the following day does not meet it on the reservation date.

## Points of judgement on the branch standard and on priority

A size that is not installed in a branch's vault cannot be reserved at that branch, whatever the customer's willingness to wait; the standard turns on what is installed, not on what is presently free.

Priority runs by reservation date within one size at one branch. Where two customers hold reservations for the same size at the same branch, the one whose reservation date is earlier is offered the box first, and this holds whichever of them is better known to the branch and whatever else either of them holds with the bank.
